proposal.utterance: Classify 'an act of promising' in BFO terms.

entities.label: ActOfPromising
entities.rationale: An act of promising is a temporally extended happening — a speech act or communicative event — that unfolds in time and involves participants. It is not a continuant; it occurs and then is over. BFO_0000015 (Process) is the correct home. It is modeled as a class because 'an act of promising' picks out a kind, not a named individual.

entities.label: Promise
entities.rationale: The promise itself — the propositional or normative content that arises from the act — is an information-like artifact that can be copied, referred to, or instantiated in different carriers (memory, written note, recorded speech). This makes it a generically dependent continuant. It is distinct from the act of promising (which is a process) just as the text of a contract is distinct from the signing event.

entities.label: PromissoryObligation
entities.rationale: The obligation that attaches to a promisor as a result of the act is an externally-grounded specifically dependent continuant that inheres in the promisor. It is a Role (BFO_0000023) because its existence is grounded in the social/relational context of the promise rather than any intrinsic physical property of the bearer. Typed as a subclass of the existing working:LegalObligation class (itself BFO_0000023) when the promise is a legal one; the open question below asks whether a purely moral reading is also needed.

relations.rationale: ActOfPromising is a kind of process — it unfolds in time.
The promise-content is a generically dependent continuant: an information object that depends on some bearer but can be multiply instantiated.
A promissory obligation is a species of legal/normative obligation already in the ontology; reusing working:LegalObligation as parent avoids redundancy.
The process of promising realizes (brings into being) the promissory obligation that the promisor then bears. BFO_0000055 (realizes) links a process to the realizable entity it actualizes.
The act of promising has the promise-content as a participant in the sense that the GDC (promise content) is concretized in and through the process.

open_questions: Should 'PromissoryObligation' be restricted to legal promises (contracts), or should it also cover purely moral/social promises? If the latter, a separate 'MoralPromissoryObligation' class typed under BFO_0000023 but not under working:LegalObligation may be needed.

Is the intended scope of 'ActOfPromising' limited to speech acts (utterances), or does it include written or implicit promises? This affects whether subclasses (VerbalActOfPromising, WrittenActOfPromising) should be introduced.
Should 'Promise' (the content) be further typed as a subclass of working:LegalForm or working:Statute when it takes legal effect, or remain a standalone GDC class?
proposal.rationale_summary: An act of promising decomposes cleanly into three BFO-grounded entities: (1) the process of promising (ActOfPromising, BFO_0000015), which is the temporally bounded communicative event; (2) the promise content (Promise, BFO_0000031), which is the generically dependent information-object — the propositional commitment — that the act produces and that can be re-instantiated in different carriers; and (3) the promissory obligation (PromissoryObligation, BFO_0000023), a role that the process realizes and that subsequently inheres in the promisor. This tripartite structure respects BFO's continuant/occurrent divide: the act is an occurrent, the content and the obligation are continuants of different dependency types. The existing working:LegalObligation class is reused as the parent of PromissoryObligation to maintain coherence with the existing ontology.
